PR title: test(tmux): replace the provider waiver with an executable conformance proof

PR description:
## What this changes

The built-in tmux runtime now has an executable conformance proof instead of a time-bounded waiver. Its existing integration suite runs the shared runtime-provider contract directly against the production `NewSeamBackedWithConfig` constructor, and the checked provider ledger names that exact test as its proof.

The proof remains isolated from a user's tmux environment: every conformance session uses the package test socket and the package's existing cleanup ownership. The integration environment is responsible for providing tmux, so the proof no longer silently skips for short mode, a missing executable, or a degraded start.

## Review notes

- Confirm the factory shape remains intentionally direct so the provider-ledger validator can trace the production constructor.
- Confirm `tmuxConformanceConfig` continues to select `testSocketName`; no changed command should address the default tmux server.
- The 250 ms nudge-idle timeout is test-only and covers the conformance fixture's fallback path without changing production defaults.

## Test plan

- [x] Run the full 40-job local CI union with rootless Podman; all tmux shards and the diff-owned proof pass.
- [x] Run `TestTmuxConformance` directly with the integration tag against real tmux; all provider-contract subtests pass with no skips.
- [x] Run `TestCatalogMatchesProductionWiringAndDocumentation`; the exact proof reference and generated ledger are synchronized.
- [x] Run CI policy, lint, vet, documentation, formatting, and push-gate checks.
- [x] Release gate: [`release-gates/ga-uz5t3a-4-tmux-provider-proof-gate.md`](release-gates/ga-uz5t3a-4-tmux-provider-proof-gate.md)
